proof_scope: In progress. R1749 paid blank-start prefix,input reset and zero-slack native CutIneq remain verified. R1750 proves exact bit-plane simulation for every original Transpose.TM M, with no restriction on its work alphabet, number of tapes, input contents, or time bound. Let ell=max(1,Nat.size M.g). BitPlaneMachine.machine M uses M.k*ell tapes,5 symbols and the same state count. Every source transition is exactly one target transition; initial blanks, input moves, output, halting, all partial stepN executions and frozen runs are preserved. Each source work-head trajectory is replicated on its ell planes. For every w,out,t, ComputesWithin(converted M,w,out,t) iff ComputesWithin(M,w,out,t). TransposesWithin with the identical time function follows. The code and decoder are executable finite tables depending only on M.g; zero encodes as all blank. No arithmetic on input-size words is hidden in a unit-cost instruction. This is standard alphabet normalization used to cover arbitrary payloads, with no novelty claim. The arbitrary payload has not yet been composed with PaidReady.
